tool_input.content:
Incident: KubePodCrashLooping, shop namespace, cluster kind-aurora-lab (2026-10-02).

Root cause: ConfigMap `frontend-nginx` (mounted at /etc/nginx/conf.d in the `frontend` deployment) contained a typo directive `proxy_conect_timeout` (missing 'n', should be `proxy_connect_timeout`). nginx validates its full config at startup and exits 1 with `nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout"` on any new pod start.

Trigger mechanism: The typo had been sitting in the ConfigMap without causing issues because existing pods' nginx processes don't re-read conf.d after mount sync — only fresh container starts read it. A `kubectl rollout restart deployment/frontend` (visible via `template.metadata.annotations.kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt`) forced new pods, which immediately hit the bad config and crash-looped. Old ReplicaSet pods kept serving traffic fine, so service was NOT fully down — just the rollout was wedged, which is why severity was "high" not "critical".

**Why this matters:** ConfigMap edits are NOT validated by Kubernetes and NOT versioned/rollback-able like Deployments. A bad ConfigMap can sit latent until the next pod restart/rollout exposes it, making the "what changed" investigation point to the rollout restart first — but the restart is just the trigger, the real change is the ConfigMap edit that happened earlier.

**How to apply:** For CrashLoopBackOff pods right after a `rollout restart` with no deployment template/image diff, check mounted ConfigMaps/Secrets content and the crashing container's logs for config-parse errors before assuming code/image regression. Fix is to correct the ConfigMap content (no restart needed after — kubelet's existing backoff retry will pick up the corrected volume content automatically). `kubectl rollout undo` only reverts pod template fields (annotations/image/etc), not ConfigMap data, so it's a valid quick mitigation (stops the churn, reverts to prior working RS) but doesn't fix the underlying bad config — must still patch the ConfigMap.

thoughts.content: Let me start by checking history for similar incidents and memory for this cluster/service before diving into live data.

No prior incident history/memory for "shop" service. This is the current incident itself (same one being investigated). Cluster found: kind-aurora-lab (cluster_id kubeconfig-331ba13b0c76b694). Hypothesis: a frontend pod in shop namespace is crash-looping due to a recent config change (per alert description) — need to find pod status, crash reason, and what config changed.

Finding: There are TWO frontend ReplicaSets — frontend-76d98597b9 (old, 2 pods Running fine) and frontend-7d466b6bcc (new, created 64s ago, 1 pod CrashLoopBackOff on container nginx, now in BackOff). This confirms a deployment rollout (config change) just happened to deployment/frontend, creating a new RS that is failing while the old RS continues running — consistent with alert description "restarting after a config change."

Hypothesis: new revision has a bad nginx config (e.g. broken configmap mount or syntax error) causing nginx to exit on start. Let me check the pod logs, describe, and the deployment config/configmap diff.

CONFIRMED root cause found: nginx fails to start with explicit error — nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9. This is a typo (proxy_conect_timeout instead of proxy_connect_timeout) in the config mounted from ConfigMap frontend-nginx. The pod has annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: 2026-10-02T17:17:43-04:00, confirming a rollout was triggered right as this bad config landed — matching the alert's "restarting after a config change."

Final Summary

Root cause (CONFIRMED): The frontend deployment's mounted ConfigMap frontend-nginx contains a typo — proxy_conect_timeout instead of proxy_connect_timeout — in default.conf line 9. nginx fails config validation on startup and exits with code 1: nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9. This was exposed when a kubectl rollout restart deployment/frontend (at 2026-10-02T21:17:43Z) forced creation of new pods under ReplicaSet frontend-7d466b6bcc, which read the already-bad ConfigMap fresh at startup and crash-looped. The pre-existing ReplicaSet (frontend-76d98597b9, 2/2 Running) never re-reads the config and continues serving traffic normally — so the shop frontend is currently still available, but the rollout is wedged churning restarts, which is what fired the alert.

Ruled out: resource exhaustion (CPU/mem usage trivial across all pods, well under limits), node problems (all 3 nodes Ready), image pull issues (image already present, pulled successfully), and full service outage (old pods actively serving 200s on /healthz and /api/items).

Recommended fixes (not executed — read-only mode):
Fix-forward: Correct the ConfigMap typo (proxy_conect_timeout → proxy_connect_timeout). No restart needed — the crashing pod's existing backoff retry will succeed once the volume content is corrected.
Immediate mitigation: kubectl rollout undo deployment/frontend -n shop — reverts to revision 1 (verified Available), stopping the crash-loop churn, but does not fix the underlying ConfigMap and must be followed by the ConfigMap patch.
